In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance concept has been of minor concern in the choice of materials in building construction.
the energy consumption of building materials and buildings is a complex problem.

the use of building materials has been guided by a number of factors: • Availability of materials and the cost of transportation • Cost of materials and labour • Performance of materials over time • Performance of materials under use • Environmental aspects • Social aspects • Cultural aspects • Aesthetic aspects The choice of materials has been guided to a varying extent by the factors above.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been able to demonstrate that a number of the materials that are used in building today are not suitable for the long term.
the energy consumption of buildings has been reduced by 50% during the last 50 years, and the energy consumption of building construction has been reduced by about 30% (see Fig. 1).
we have developed a new approach to the selection of building materials based on performance and life-cycle costs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no single best material for all applications.
there is a need for a more holistic approach to the selection of building materials, taking into account the total costs of ownership, and that the life cycle perspective is a key to this.
